val alpha = (PI.toFloat() * slitWidthM * sin(thetaRad)) / wavelengthM

mystery.en: Why does shining light through two narrow slits produce dark bands where you expect brightness?

en.title: Young's Double-Slit & Wave Fringes
en.teaser: Coherent laser light diffracted through twin slits forms a brilliant array of alternating bright and dark fringes.

en.hook: How can shooting light through two slits create alternating bands of darkness where light should be?
en.math: Wave crests and troughs from twin slits superpose, constructively boosting intensity where paths align, and canceling into complete darkness where they differ by half a wavelength.
en.question: Can we simulate Young's double-slit interference and diffraction live in Kotlin Multiplatform?
en.code_tip: We compute wavefront phase delays, apply the single-slit sinc envelope, and render interference fringes on Canvas.
en.payoff: Young's double-slit wave interference and intensity fringes running live in Kotlin.
